q: More than 3 billion people depend on marine and coastal biodiversity, while more than _____ billion people rely on forests for their livelihoods.
e: More than 3 billion people depend on marine and coastal biodiversity, while more than 1.6 billion people rely on forests for their livelihoods. So we write 1.6. Leave 2.6 and 3.6 out.

q: The loss of biodiversity affects the lives of more than _____ billion people living in dry lands.
e: The loss of biodiversity affects the lives of more than 1 billion people living in dry lands. The blank is 1. Not 3 or 2.

q: Which of the following is NOT listed as one of the five major threats to biodiversity?
e: The answer is captive breeding. There are five major threats to biodiversity. Not habitat loss or climate change.

q: The clearing of land for agriculture, housing, transport, leisure facilities and industry removes vegetation, leading to habitat _____.
e: The clearing of land for agriculture, housing, transport, leisure facilities and industry removes vegetation, leading to habitat fragmentation. Fragmentation is the word, not restoration or expansion.

q: Physically larger species and those living at lower latitudes or in forests or oceans are more sensitive to reduction in habitat _____.
e: Physically larger species and those living at lower latitudes or in forests or oceans are more sensitive to reduction in habitat area. The blank is area. Not quality or connectivity.

q: Which of the following is a major reason for habitat destruction mentioned in the text?
e: The answer is dam construction. Shifting cultivation in upland areas and gold mining are major reasons for habitat destruction in Myanmar. Not seed banking or captive breeding.

q: Factors such as the replacement of local landraces with modern varieties and overgrazing are major threats to the _____ of Myanmar.
e: Factors such as the replacement of local landraces with modern varieties and overgrazing are major threats to the agrobiodiversity of Myanmar. The blank is agrobiodiversity. Not marine biodiversity or ex situ conservation.

q: Pollution is caused by uncontrolled pesticide and herbicide uses, various factory wastes, different kinds of rubbish, human sewage, radioactive materials and _____.
e: Pollution is caused by uncontrolled pesticide and herbicide uses, various factory wastes, different kinds of rubbish, human sewage, radioactive materials and industrial wastes. Industrial wastes is the word, not organic fertilizers or compost.

q: Invasive alien species (IAS) can be introduced unintentionally by tourists or through the transport of cargo or movement of pets, plant parts and _____.
e: Invasive alien species (IAS) can be introduced unintentionally by tourists or through the transport of cargo or movement of pets, plant parts and seeds. So we write seeds. Leave water and soil out.

q: Some invasive alien species may be intentionally imported for use in research, manufacture of medicine or ornamental and _____ uses.
e: Some invasive alien species may be intentionally imported for use in research, manufacture of medicine or ornamental and industrial uses. The blank is industrial. Not agricultural or medical.

q: Genetic pollution indicates the loss of identity of wild plant species as a result of transfer of genes from _____.
e: Genetic pollution indicates the loss of identity of wild plant species as a result of transfer of genes from crop plants. The blank is crop plants. Not wild animals or invasive species.

q: Gene flow is expected to have its greatest effect on weed species that are closely related to crop plants taxonomically, ecologically and in their reproductive _____.
e: Gene flow is expected to have its greatest effect on weed species that are closely related to crop plants taxonomically, ecologically and in their reproductive biology. The blank is biology. Not isolation or barriers.

q: The term 'genetic pollution' is usually associated with the gene flow from a genetically engineered organism to a _____ organism.
e: The term 'genetic pollution' is usually associated with the gene flow from a genetically engineered organism to a non-GE organism. Non-GE is the word, not transgenic or modified.

q: Overexploitation, also called overharvesting, can lead to the destruction of the resource, as it will be unable to _____.
e: Overexploitation, also called overharvesting, can lead to the destruction of the resource, as it will be unable to replenish. Replenish is the word, not adapt or evolve.

q: Overfishing is the removal of a species of fish from a body of water at a rate greater than that the species can replenish its population _____.
e: Overfishing is the removal of a species of fish from a body of water at a rate greater than that the species can replenish its population naturally. So we write naturally. Leave artificially and rapidly out.

q: Overlogging is a form of overexploitation caused by legal or illegal logging activities that lead to unsustainable or irrecoverable deforestation and permanent habitat destruction for forest _____.
e: Overlogging is a form of overexploitation caused by legal or illegal logging activities that lead to unsustainable or irrecoverable deforestation and permanent habitat destruction for forest wildlife. So we write wildlife. Leave soils and water out.

q: Overhunting threatens _____ of endangered vertebrates, as well as other groups.
e: Overhunting threatens one-third of endangered vertebrates, as well as other groups. The blank is one-third. Not one-half or two-thirds.

q: Excluding edible fish, the illegal trade in wildlife is valued at $_____ billion per year.
e: Excluding edible fish, the illegal trade in wildlife is valued at $10 billion per year. So we write 10. Leave 20 and 5 out.

q: Bushmeat provides increased opportunity for transmission of several zoonotic viruses from animal hosts to humans, such as Ebola virus and _____.
e: Bushmeat provides increased opportunity for transmission of several zoonotic viruses from animal hosts to humans, such as Ebola virus and HIV. HIV is the word, not malaria or dengue.

q: Climate change alters the climate patterns and ecosystems in which species have evolved and on which they _____.
e: Climate change alters the climate patterns and ecosystems in which species have evolved and on which they depend. Depend is the word, not feed or prey.

q: Rising ocean temperatures and diminishing Arctic sea ice affects marine biodiversity and can shift _____ zones.
e: Rising ocean temperatures and diminishing Arctic sea ice affects marine biodiversity and can shift vegetation zones. Vegetation is the word, not trophic or precipitation.

q: An increase in the world's population will cause additional strains on resources, leading to more deforestation, decreased biodiversity, and spikes in pollution and _____.
e: An increase in the world's population will cause additional strains on resources, leading to more deforestation, decreased biodiversity, and spikes in pollution and emissions. Emissions is the word, not conservation or recycling.

q: Wildlife trade refers to the commerce of products that are derived from non-domesticated animals or plants usually extracted from their natural environment or raised under controlled _____.
e: Wildlife trade refers to the commerce of products that are derived from non-domesticated animals or plants usually extracted from their natural environment or raised under controlled conditions. Conditions is the word, not habitats or reserves.

q: Recent overexploitation of wildlife for trade has affected countless species driven by high demand from expanding illegal wildlife markets in _____ countries.
e: Recent overexploitation of wildlife for trade has affected countless species driven by high demand from expanding illegal wildlife markets in neighboring countries. So we write neighboring. Leave western and developed out.

q: In wildlife smuggling, much of demand for rhinoceros' horns, tiger bones, and other animal products arises out of the practice of traditional _____ medicine.
e: In wildlife smuggling, much of demand for rhinoceros' horns, tiger bones, and other animal products arises out of the practice of traditional chinese medicine. Chinese is the word, not ayurvedic or western.

q: The most trafficked animal in the world is the pangolin, accounting for as much as _____% of all illegal wildlife trade.
e: The most trafficked animal in the world is the pangolin, accounting for as much as 20%% of all illegal wildlife trade. So we write 20%. Leave 10% and 50% out.

q: In the last decade, more than one million pangolins were poached and killed for their _____.
e: In the last decade, more than one million pangolins were poached and killed for their scales. The blank is scales. Not meat or bones.

q: Wildlife smuggling may cause the introduction of invasive and harmful species into an ecosystem, which can endanger indigenous wildlife by putting a strain on the environment's resources through interspecific _____.
e: Wildlife smuggling may cause the introduction of invasive and harmful species into an ecosystem, which can endanger indigenous wildlife by putting a strain on the environment's resources through interspecific competition. Competition is the word, not cooperation or symbiosis.

q: Outbreaks of zoonotic diseases including COVID-19, H5N1 avian flu, severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), and monkeypox have been traced to live wildlife _____.
e: Outbreaks of zoonotic diseases including COVID-19, H5N1 avian flu, severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), and monkeypox have been traced to live wildlife markets. So we write markets. Leave farms and reserves out.

q: CITES stands for the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Flora and _____.
e: CITES stands for the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Flora and fauna. So we write fauna. Leave fungi and fish out.

q: The Conservation of Biodiversity and Protected Areas Law was enacted in Myanmar in the year _____.
e: The Conservation of Biodiversity and Protected Areas Law was enacted in Myanmar in the year 2018. 2018 is the word, not 2015 or 2020.

q: Certain places in the world where wildlife trade is particularly threatening or where targeted action would be particularly worthwhile are called 'wildlife trade _____.
e: Certain places in the world where wildlife trade is particularly threatening or where targeted action would be particularly worthwhile are called 'wildlife trade hotspots. So we write hotspots. Leave zones and centers out.

q: Excessive use of fertilizers and industrial and domestic forms of _____ is one of the five major threats to biodiversity.
e: Excessive use of fertilizers and industrial and domestic forms of pollution is one of the five major threats to biodiversity. So we write pollution. Leave waste and chemicals out.

q: The effects of invasive alien species on native species and especially _____ is a major threat to biodiversity.
e: The effects of invasive alien species on native species and especially endemics is a major threat to biodiversity. Endemics is the word, not exotics or migratories.
